clue.text: Money — a note, say

indicators.note: say signals that the note is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: doh is the first note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Cash described as a banknote, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a note, say' looks like an example of money (a banknote), but it is the musical note DOH, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough is slang for cash.

clue.text: Protest against fall in value, dropping one

indicators.note: dropping tells us a piece is let fall from the longer word

parts.note: to depreciate is to fall in value
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a currency's slide in value, which has lost a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes I (one) from DEPRECIATE; the two words are often confused, which the surface exploits.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprecate is to express disapproval of something.

clue.text: Distress, being ahead on several games

parts.note: a player who is ahead is said to be up
a set in tennis is a group of several games

explanation.surface: A player is distressed even while leading over a number of games.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone is to cause them distress.

clue.text: Here are the main points of the news

definitions.text: Here are the main points of the news

parts.words: Here are the main points of the news
parts.note: a bulletin opens with a summary of its top stories, and a newspaper's top lines announce each story

explanation.definitionFit: Headlines summarise the most important news items at the start of a bulletin.

clue.text: Englishman puts sticks back in. the window-frame

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a sash is the sliding frame of a sash window

indicators.note: back means the word for sticks is read from right to left

parts.note: canes are walking sticks

explanation.surface: An Englishman replaces some rods in a window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CANES into SENAC, which goes 'in' SASH. Sassenach is a Scots word, often teasing, for an English person.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassenach is the Scottish and Irish term for a person from England.

clue.text: He knows a lot about central heating from the sun

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: solar means coming from the sun

explanation.surface: An expert explains how solar energy can run home heating.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person with deep knowledge.

clue.text: Post a GP. arranged for a locum

indicators.note: arranged means these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone posts a family doctor elsewhere to cover as a temporary substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor in Britain; the doctor theme makes 'locum' feel like part of the scene rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a temporary stand-in, which is what a stopgap is.

clue.text: This appears to be Latin name for a German town.

parts.note: esse is the Latin infinitive meaning to be

explanation.surface: A town's name in Germany looks as if it were the Latin for existence.
explanation.walkthrough: ESSE is Latin for 'to be' (as in 'in esse'); add N for name. Essen is a city in the Ruhr.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in western Germany.

clue.text: Have canal altered by heavy downfall.

indicators.note: altered means these letters are changed into another order

explanation.surface: A canal has been changed by a severe storm.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is a massive fall of snow down a mountainside.

clue.text: Worry Hotspur

explanation.surface: An anxious soldier named for a famous fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to harass; Hotspur was the nickname of Sir Henry (Harry) Percy, in Shakespeare's Henry IV.

clue.text: Nut disintegrates as I chop it

indicators.note: disintegrates means the letters fall apart and are reformed

explanation.surface: A cook chops a nut and it falls to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The pistachio is a green-kernelled edible seed.

clue.text: Step with thanks into a title

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone moves up into a noble rank, grateful for the honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is a single step in a flight.

clue.text: Former tax said to crack up

indicators.note: said shows the phrase is spoken to give a word of like sound

parts.note: ex means former, and a toll is a tax or charge

explanation.surface: An abolished levy is said to be falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack up' is not 'collapse' here but the idiom 'crack up' meaning praise highly, as in 'not all it's cracked up to be'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cracked up is to be praised, and to extol is to praise lavishly.

clue.text: Fabulous sort of green lady

indicators.note: sort of means these letters are made into a different form

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale woman in green.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabulous in its root sense means belonging to fable or legend.

clue.text: First, of many' taken in by a solitary social worker

indicators.note: taken in by means the first letter is held inside the other piece

parts.note: a loner is a solitary person

indicators.note: First points to the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A recluse takes in the first of many who need help.
explanation.walkthrough: An almoner was a hospital social worker in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically an almoner was a hospital's medical social worker.

clue.text: Made ready ones in-the crowd I headed

parts.note: a mob is an unruly crowd

indicators.note: in means one piece sits within the others

parts.note: led means headed, as a leader does
IS is the plural of I, the Roman one

explanation.surface: A rabble-rouser readied the people they led.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ones' is the plural of the Roman one, and 'in' places it after the L of the word for headed, so the leader's word is split rather than kept whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To mobilise troops is to make them ready for action.

clue.text: Bill follows Peter — he, shows, dashing style'

indicators.note: follows tells us the account piece comes after the name

parts.note: Peter Pan is the boy who never grew up
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A man after Peter shows real flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence or flair.

clue.text: In a month New' Mexico replaces five;'one not belonging..:

indicators.note: replaces means one letter is swapped out for another pair

parts.note: November is a month
V is the Roman numeral for five
NM is the postal abbreviation for New Mexico

explanation.surface: During a particular month, a US state takes over and someone is left out.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsider not in a club or group is a nonmember.

clue.text: Such a capital fellow, Burlington Bertie. originally

definitions.text: Such a capital fellow, Burlington Bertie. originally

parts.words: Such a capital fellow, Burlington Bertie. originally
parts.note: Burlington Bertie from Bow, in the music-hall song, came from Bow in the poorer part of London, the capital

explanation.walkthrough: Burlington Bertie of the music-hall song was 'from Bow', in London's East End; 'capital fellow' means a Londoner, not a good chap.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of London's East End is a Cockney Londoner.

clue.text: The home of excellency

parts.note: an ambassador is addressed as Your Excellency, so the official residence is where an excellency lives

explanation.definitionFit: An embassy is an ambassador's official residence.

clue.text: With fluttering eyelid leader of damsels submitted

indicators.note: fluttering means the letters move about into a new order
leader of points to the opening letter of the word after

explanation.surface: A damsel bats her eyelid and gives in.
explanation.definitionFit: To have yielded is to have given way or surrendered.

clue.text: Admit to. study the band of ' heraldry

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a fess is a broad horizontal band across a heraldic shield

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to examining a coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: To confess is to acknowledge or own up to something.

clue.text: Lover's-heart as" worn on the sleeve

definitions.text: Lover's-heart as" worn on the sleeve

parts.words: Lover's-heart as" worn on the sleeve
parts.note: the middle letter of lover is V, and a V-shaped stripe is worn on a uniform sleeve, echoing wearing one's heart on one's sleeve

explanation.walkthrough: The heart of 'loVer' is V; a V-shaped stripe on a uniform sleeve marks rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevron is a V-shaped stripe on a sleeve showing rank.

clue.text: Italian globe — one's. spinning

indicators.note: spinning means the letters turn about into another order

parts.note: the letters of one's are used, the s included

explanation.surface: A globe and its owner rotate.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolognese means from Bologna, a city in Italy.

clue.text: Words of praise make you light up right inside

indicators.note: inside means one letter sits within the other piece
up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a bulb is an electric light

explanation.surface: Flattering comments make you glow with pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns BULB into BLUB; R goes 'inside' to give BL-U-R-B.
explanation.definitionFit: A blurb is promotional praise printed on a book jacket.

clue.text: One in, say, exalted spirits ()

indicators.note: exalted means raised, so in a down entry the whole run is read upwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
EG (for example) means say

explanation.surface: A person, perhaps, among those in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exalted' raises the whole of I + IN + EG, giving GE-NI-I read down.
explanation.definitionFit: Genii is a plural of genie, a magical spirit.

clue.text: Destroy. before admitting ancient copper.

indicators.note: admitting means the first piece lets the second in

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before
the as was a Roman copper coin

explanation.surface: Someone wrecks a relic, having first let in an old coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to wipe out or obliterate.

clue.text: Serve as a cover, they say

indicators.note: they say shows the phrase is spoken to give another word of like sound

parts.note: a veil is a cover for the face

explanation.surface: Something reportedly acts as a covering.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to be of use or help.

clue.text: Abram, the. Canadian. porcupine

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Abram, the. Canadian. porcupine': 'Abram' gives no wordplay for URSON (the Canadian porcupine); likely an OCR garble with no scan to correct it.

clue.text: It's figured as a target

parts.note: figured means marked with numbers, as the scoring segments around a round board are

explanation.definitionFit: A dartboard is a numbered circular target for darts.

clue.text: Ordered about a: sort of red unable to get up

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: bidden means ordered or commanded

indicators.note: sort of means these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient was told to lie still, unable to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' shuffles the colour word into EDR, and 'about' means the word for ordered goes round it, split after its first letter. 'a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedridden person is confined to bed by illness.

clue.text: Governor, one draw the line somewhere

explanation.surface: A governor who knows where the limits are.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler governs a country; a ruler is also a straight edge used to draw lines.
